Licence comparison

Three courses, each with its own page for the detail.

CourseWhat it coversUsual starting point
Category CRigid lorries over 3.5 tonnes.Usually a category B car licence, plus a lorry medical and the theory tests.
Category C+EArticulated lorries and drawbar combinations.Category C is the usual licence held before this training.
Driver CPCA professional qualification for lorry and bus drivers. It is not a vehicle category.Depends on whether you need initial or periodic CPC.

Which licence is right for me?

A quick guide. We check the licence you already hold when you enquire.

  • Category CThe usual route onto a rigid lorry if you hold a car licence and want to drive goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes.
  • Category C+EThe trailer licence, for articulated lorries and drawbar combinations, once you hold Category C.
  • Driver CPCThe professional qualification that goes alongside your licence for many paid driving jobs. It doesn't replace Category C or C+E.
Ask which licence fits

Typical training journey

What to expect, from your first enquiry to training day.

  1. Tell us what you want to drive

    Category C, Category C+E or Driver CPC. If you're not sure, say so and we'll talk it through.

  2. We check what you already hold

    We look at your current licence and explain any medical, theory or CPC steps that go alongside the practical training.

  3. Train from our local base

    Practical sessions run from our single training base. We agree dates with you once you've enquired.

  4. Prepare for what comes next

    That might be your practical test or periodic CPC hours. We explain how booking works when you get in touch.

What training includes

Each course page sets out the practical work in detail. In short:

  • Category CPractical training for rigid lorries over 3.5 tonnes, for drivers moving up from a car licence.
  • Category C+ETrailer training for drivers who already hold Category C and want to drive articulated or drawbar lorries.
  • Driver CPCPeriodic training for professional drivers who need hours towards their five-year Driver CPC requirement.

Costs and pricing

We don't publish a fixed price list, because the right training depends on the licence you hold and how much practice you need. Ask for a quote for the course you want. Medical, theory test and practical test fees are separate costs, and we explain them when we quote.

Common questions

What is the difference between Category C and Category C+E?

Category C is the rigid lorry licence. Category C+E adds a trailer, for articulated lorries and drawbar combinations. C+E training normally follows Category C.

Is Driver CPC the same as an HGV licence?

No. Category C and Category C+E are vehicle licences. Driver CPC is a professional qualification for drivers who need a Driver Qualification Card.

Can you tell me if I'm eligible?

Not from a web page. This is general guidance. We check the licence you hold when you enquire and tell you what applies to you.

Why don't you list prices?

The right training depends on the licence you already hold and how much practice you need, so we quote for each learner individually. Ask for a quote for the course you want.
